sections.content: How many people are "footwear and leather working trades"?

6,845 people

were counted on the census as "footwear and leather working trades" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Footwear and leather working trades make and repair shoes, cut out, make up, sew, decorate and finish leather and leather substitute goods other than garments.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "footwear and leather working trades" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "footwear and leather working trades", 13.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "footwear and leather working trades" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "footwear and leather working trades" included:

  • metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations
  • sheet metal workers
  • textiles, garments and related trades (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "footwear and leather working trades" there were more men than women (65.5% compared with 34.5%).

This means "footwear and leather working trades" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 65.5% and women made up 34.5% of "footwear and leather working trades"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "footwear and leather working trades" included:

  • IT project managers
  • police officers (sergeant and below)
  • directors in consultancy services

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "footwear and leather working trades" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "footwear and leather working trades" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "footwear and leather working trades", 11.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (73.1% compared with 26.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (74.4%) than self-employed (25.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the East Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included West Northamptonshire, this is in the same region of the East Midlands.
